title: Why Your Edge Model Fails After Deployment
story: a model that scored 98% in the lab meets a real factory camera, and the fix is in the data, not the architecture

scenes.name: The moment
scenes.spoken: Your model scores ninety-eight percent in the lab, so you ship it to the factory camera. A week later, it's missing half the defects.
scenes.visual: Laptop mockup with a lime accuracy chart at 98%, then a camera tile; the chart line drops red as missed-defect markers appear.

scenes.name: The turn
scenes.onscreen: The lab never saw the glare
scenes.spoken: Here's what changed. The lab photos were clean, but the factory has glare, dust, and a camera that shakes a little every time the belt moves.
scenes.visual: Split view: clean lab image tile vs factory image tile; glare, dust, and shake icons pop onto the factory side.

scenes.name: The lesson and next step
scenes.onscreen: Test the slice, not the average
scenes.spoken: So before you swap architectures, collect a few hundred frames from the real camera and test on those first. Follow for more.
scenes.visual: Frames stream from the camera tile into a test set card; a per-slice bar chart shows the glare slice recovering. End card with avatar.

sources: Replace with verified sources, one per claim, with links.
